subject: Follow-up: FinPay competitive TCO & next tests (per-1M tokens, batching, cache)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Rogers <jamie.rogers@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: FinPay competitive TCO & next tests (per-1M tokens, batching, cache)

Jamie — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps after our discovery / competitive evaluation call: 

Recap (what we heard)
- FinPay runs a mix of short transactional prompts (charges, refunds) and longer customer-support summarization. Estimated steady-state: ~2M tokens/day, spiky bursts up to 10M/day.
- Primary evaluation criteria: latency p95 (<250ms), cost per 1M tokens, and integration ease (auth, VPC).
- Current incumbent: Hyperscaler-managed LLM endpoints + internal caching layer. Interest in comparing unit economics and fallback behavior.

Redwood differentiation (short)
- Lower per-token unit cost at production scale via batching + KV/prefix caching and quantized variants.
- Smart routing to fall back to cheaper model variant for non-critical inference without degrading customer UX.
- Clear cost controls (per-route SLOs, autoscaling with reserved pools) and enterprise telemetry.

Initial TCO numbers (high level) — ballpark (we'll share workbook attached)
- Per-1M tokens, short prompts (avg length ~30 tokens): Redwood hosted (with batching + 60% cache hit) ~ $18–22 per 1M tokens.
- Hyperscaler managed endpoint (no caching, equivalent model): ~ $35–45 per 1M tokens.
- Differences driven by: batching (10–20% savings at 100 concurrency), KV cache (reduces tokens billed on average by hit rate), and larger quantized model variants (20–30% GPU cost reduction).

Proposed next tests (to run in parallel)
1) Unit-cost measurement: 100k warm requests with your representative prompts (we'll run against Redwood-optimized variant and hyperscaler baseline). Goal: measure per-1M-token billing equivalent and end-to-end latency.
2) Latency SLO check: p95 measured at your traffic shape (p50/p95/p99).
3) Cache hit-rate simulation: run a 1M token pass with representative repeat queries to validate realistic cache hit rates (you mentioned expected ~55–65% reuse for transactional prompts).
4) Integration checklist: validate VPC peering and KMS flow for key material (security team step).

Attachments: redwood_cost_model.xlsx (TCO workbook), redwood_tco_summary.pdf (one-pager).

Next steps
- If this plan sounds good, can you share a small sample of representative prompt traces (anonymized) and your preferred week for the unit-cost run?
- I'll loop Marcus for the technical run scheduling and Marissa for procurement prep.

Thanks — happy to jump on another 30m to align test details.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0110

---
From: Jamie Rogers <jamie.rogers@finpay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: FinPay competitive TCO & next tests (per-1M tokens, batching, cache)

Thanks Aditya — nice recap. A couple quick clarifications before we move to tests: 

1) The incumbent numbers I quoted earlier are blended across multiple models; for a fair apples-to-apples we need you to use the same model family (we currently test on gptx-small equivalent). Can Redwood run the unit-cost test against that model family or a close-functioning open variant?

2) For caching: our cache layer is at the application side today with ~40% effective savings (we've measured). Your 60% assumption is higher than our data — where does that come from?

3) Security: our security team will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and confirmation that logs for inference requests can be retained for 90 days for audit purposes. Is that reasonable?

Happy to share an anonymized prompt sample (I'll get it to you later today). Prefer week of 3/16 for the test runs.

-Jamie

> Jamie — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps after our discovery / competitive evaluation call: 
> 
> [snip]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Rogers <jamie.rogers@finpay.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T12:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: FinPay competitive TCO & next tests (per-1M tokens, batching, cache)

Jamie — great questions. Short answers inline and action items below.

1) Model family: yes — we can run tests against a close open-equivalent to your gptx-small baseline (we typically use the rdx-small-open variant for benchmarking). We'll also run against our quantized rdx-small-q4 to show delta. If you prefer a hosted hyperscaler baseline, we can include that in the run.

2) Cache hit-rate assumption: our 60% figure was a conservative estimate based on typical transactional workflows we've seen from payments customers (prefix reuse + user history). But we should validate against your traces — please send the anonymized sample. Even at 40% cache hit the unit economics still show material delta once batching and quantization are included.

3) SOC 2 + logs: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report + evidence. For audit log retention, Redwood can retain inference logs for 90 days in your dedicated retention bucket with encryption; we will document the export process for auditors. I'll have our security lead share the specific SOC2 artifacts once you confirm.

Proposed experiment matrix (short)
- Baseline A: FinPay traces -> hyperscaler-managed endpoint (gptx-small)
- Baseline B: FinPay traces -> Redwood rdx-small-open (no quant)
- Variant: Redwood rdx-small-q4 (quantized) with caching enabled + batching at concurrency 50

Metrics to collect
- Effective billed tokens (with cache), cost per 1M tokens
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (end-to-end)
- GPU utilization and throughput (tokens/sec)
- Cache hit-rate observed

Scheduling / asks
- Please upload anonymized traces to the Drive link: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1FinPay-TCO-Recap or share a secure S3 (we accept short-term presigned links).
- Preferred test window: week of 2026-03-16. Marcus — can you own scheduling the infra run? Marissa — can you prep a quick order form for a short POC (1 month reserved pool)?

I'll attach the cost workbook we discussed.

Best,
Aditya

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jamie Rogers <jamie.rogers@finpay.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: FinPay competitive TCO & next tests (per-1M tokens, batching, cache)

Thanks — I'll take point on the infra runs. Quick operational notes: 

- I've provisioned a dedicated POC pool (small) and attached the preliminary cost model we used to size it (redwood_cost_model.xlsx). The model includes assumptions for token billing, batching efficiency, and cache hit delta.
- For the unit-cost run we'll need:
  * Anonymized traces in CSV (timestamp, prompt_id, prompt_text_length) or NDJSON.
  * Expected concurrency profile (requests/sec over 10 min windows) so we can model batching.
  * Approval for inbound VPC peering (if you want VPC mode) — network team will need a contact.

Operationally, we'll run three 2-hour buckets (baseline, rdx-open, rdx-q4+cache) during the week of 3/16 and deliver a short report within 48 hours of completion. If results look good we can scope an initial reserved commit (1 month) for live traffic.

Jamie — who should I coordinate with for the SPOC on networking? Also, please confirm the anonymized trace upload method.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_cost_model.xlsx
